clue.text: Timer doesn't open security device

indicators.note: a word that doesn't open has lost its opening letter

parts.note: a clock is a device that keeps time

explanation.surface: A timer that fails to start on a security system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't open' looks like a fault in the timer; it tells you to drop the first letter of CLOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A lock is a mechanism fastening doors and safes, so it is a device for keeping things secure.

clue.text: Messed-up girl shouted at male, possibly over ninety

indicators.note: something shouted is spoken out loud, so the word for girl is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: Miss is the title of a young unmarried woman
a man is a male person
someone over ninety would be called aged, elderly

explanation.surface: A confused young woman yelling at an elderly man.
explanation.walkthrough: MISS is pronounced like the prefix MIS-, which is how it enters the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mismanaged has been handled badly, so it is botched or messed up.

clue.text: Starter of samosa with considerable taste

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, punning on a samosa served as a starter

parts.note: ample means plentiful, considerable

explanation.surface: A samosa starter with plenty of flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a course in a meal; it picks the first letter S from 'samosa'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample food is to try a little of it, which is the verb taste.

clue.text: We hear little Matthew loves beastly fighters

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: little Matthew is Mat, a pet form of the name, and loves gives adores, so Mat adores

explanation.surface: Young Matthew is fond of wild fighting animals.
explanation.walkthrough: MAT ADORES spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Matadors are the bullfighters who face a bull in the ring, so their fights are with beasts.

clue.text: Lake discovered in game reserve

indicators.note: something discovered in a phrase has been found sitting within its letters

explanation.surface: A lake found inside a nature reserve for game.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'gaME REserve'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a poetic or regional word for a small lake or pond.

clue.text: Africa, for one, curtailed church's control of water

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: Africa is an example of a continent
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: African church authorities managing water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'control of water' sounds like irrigation, but it is bladder control.
explanation.definitionFit: Continence is the ability to hold in urine, which is self-control over passing water.

clue.text: Original American way of working upset China

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a method of working

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An American method of operating that has annoyed China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges CHINA into HICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohicans were a Native American people, the original inhabitants of the continent.

clue.text: Yahoo, say, backed up by secretary's young assistant

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: backed up means sent backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a yahoo is a boorish lout, a yob
say introduces an example, EG

explanation.surface: An internet company, supported by a secretary's junior helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yahoo' looks like the web firm but is a lout. YOB and EG reversed give GEBOY; a yob is British slang for a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageboy is a boy attendant, as at a wedding or formerly in a great house.

clue.text: Excellent anaesthetic like 3 perhaps

parts.note: prime means first-rate, excellent
an anaesthetic is something that numbs, a numb-er

explanation.surface: A top-quality painkiller compared to clue three.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anaesthetic' looks like a noun for a drug; read NUMBER as 'thing that numbs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is divisible only by itself and one, the property of primes; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Polar native lacks wings to make plane

indicators.note: wings are the outer edges of a word, here missing at both ends

parts.note: an Eskimo is a native of the Arctic

explanation.surface: An Arctic local without wings trying to build an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' looks like an aircraft (hence 'wings'), but it is the verb, to glide over water.
explanation.definitionFit: To plane is to glide lightly over a water surface, as a boat or stone does, which is to skim.

clue.text: Hospital department follows each person full-time

indicators.note: follows shows the department comes after the other pieces

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'
man means a person
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Every staff member in a hospital unit working full shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent job is a lasting, regular post rather than temporary, as a full-time one is.

clue.text: Criminal gang caught by Iron Curtain border?

indicators.note: caught by means held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a ring is a criminal network, as in a smuggling ring

explanation.surface: Gangsters trapped by the Iron Curtain at a Cold War frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Curtain' reads as a single phrase; split it, Iron giving FE and Curtain belonging to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe is a decorative edging of threads, as hangs along the bottom of a curtain.

clue.text: Taking back right to rise up in response

indicators.note: in puts the turned piece within the word for response

parts.note: a reaction is a response

indicators.note: in a down clue rising up reads the letters from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: Withdrawing a political right to revolt in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right to rise up' reads like a call to revolt; 'to' is only a link, and 'rise up' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A retraction withdraws a statement, the act of taking back what was said.

clue.text: Skulking low life-force's no good

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
chi is the vital life-force in Chinese thought

explanation.surface: Lurking about a lowlife whose energy is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' reads as an adjective but is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooching means loitering or slouching about aimlessly, close to skulking around.

clue.text: Memorable moments from top-class matches?

parts.note: high means superior, top-class
matches are lights, used to light a fire

explanation.surface: The best bits shown from elite sporting fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matches' looks like sporting contests but means things for striking a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: Highlights are the outstanding parts of an event, the moments most worth remembering.

clue.text: Only men party with sinister-looking guns

indicators.note: sinister means left in heraldry, so looking left means reading right to left

parts.note: gats are guns in old gangster slang

explanation.surface: A men-only celebration where the guns look menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' looks like menace but carries its Latin sense of left; GATS read leftwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party is a celebration for a groom attended only by males.

clue.text: Abolish Grammar School reports!

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit or abolish

explanation.surface: A call to scrap selective state schools, like a headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reports' looks like a noun for documents; it is loud noises. A grammar school is a selective British state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports are loud explosive noises, like gunshots, which are bangs.

clue.text: Colonies rash to support US cooperative gathering

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits below it

parts.note: a bee is a communal working gathering, like a quilting bee
hives is an itchy skin rash

explanation.surface: Communities hastily backing an American collective meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like hasty; it is the skin complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Beehives house bee colonies, so the word stands for the colonies themselves.

clue.text: Hereditary factor somewhat degenerate

indicators.note: somewhat means only part, so a piece of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An inherited trait that is a bit corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'deGENErate'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene is the unit of heredity passed from parent to offspring.

clue.text: Nightmare about dead Mary? On the contrary

indicators.note: about means round and around, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A horror dream about a dead woman named Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' stirs DEAD MARY. 'On the contrary' says the definition is the opposite of 'Nightmare'.
explanation.definitionFit: Read with the closing phrase, the definition is the opposite of a bad dream: a pleasant waking reverie.

clue.text: Verbal instruction to infuse red wine for fish

indicators.note: verbal means spoken, so the phrase counts by its sound

parts.note: to mull wine is to heat it with spices, so the instruction is 'mull it'

explanation.surface: Spoken advice to soak fish in red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: MULL IT said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Red and grey mullets are well-known edible sea fish.

clue.text: Purée that is No. 5 on today's course

parts.note: mash is food pulped into a purée
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Mashed food that's the fifth dish of today's menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a meal; it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie was an old golf club, equivalent to the five iron of modern sets.

clue.text: Shoddy quality of disorganised ski ascent

indicators.note: disorganised means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badly organised ski lift ride shows poor standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackiness is cheap, tasteless or tawdry character, the mark of shoddy goods.

clue.text: Coldplay's first album includes one film passage

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the band's name is taken
includes means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record album
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The debut record of a British band containing a movie excerpt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first album' looks like Coldplay's debut; 'first' only picks C.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a short extract from a film or broadcast, a passage of footage.

clue.text: Old German picked up French in the end

parts.note: got means obtained, picked up

indicators.note: in the end means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An ancient German learned French eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a sound signal; it just means GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Goths were an ancient Germanic people who invaded the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Smart leaders of the revolution in Moscow

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Well-dressed heads of the Russian Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' suggests Lenin and co; it takes initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim means neat and well kept in appearance, as smart does.

clue.text: Maybe yew produced fir cone

indicators.note: produced means made, so the letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: Perhaps a yew tree has borne a fir cone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' marks the yew as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The yew is an evergreen in the conifer group, though it bears berries not cones.

clue.text: Queue to see final part of Babe?

definitions.meaning: a queue is an old word for a plait of hair hanging at the back
Babe is the pig in the film, so its final part is its tail

explanation.surface: Waiting in line to watch the end of the film Babe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queue' looks like a line of people; it is a plait. Babe is the 1995 film about a pig.
explanation.definitionFit: A plait at the back of the head is a queue; a pig's curly rear appendage is the other sense.
